records.name: Tango Therapy Project
records.summary: A group that teaches adapted Argentine tango to people with Parkinson's, stroke survivors and older adults, and trains volunteers to dance alongside them.
records.what_you_do: Join a weekly tango series of about an hour and a half, with a care partner if you like. Or take the volunteer training and help dance with participants during classes.

schedule.text: Adapted tango series meet weekly for 4 to 10 weeks, about 1.5 hours a session. Parkinson's series run on Wednesday mornings in Center City and on Saturday afternoons in Cherry Hill, NJ. Older adult series run on weekday mornings and afternoons in Germantown and Stapeley. Current dates are posted on the site.

locations.label: Center City class site (First Presbyterian Church)
Cherry Hill class site (Katz JCC)
locations.address: 1301 Springdale Rd, Cherry Hill Township, NJ

locations.label: Center in the Park, Germantown (volunteer training and older adult classes)

cost.text: Class fees are not listed on the site. Volunteer training is free.

first_step.how: Register for the Cherry Hill series (starts October 10) through the site's Register link, or email hello@tangotherapyproject.org to ask about joining a series that is already under way.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to people with Parkinson's, stroke survivors and older adults, care partners are welcome, and each series has a register link or an email address. The site does not say whether late joining is allowed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class lasts about an hour and a half and includes a gentle warm-up, rhythm and balance work, partner practice, some tango steps, dancing, and time for refreshments and talk. Trained instructors lead the class, and volunteers give one-on-one support. The site does not list the class fee.
first_visit_tips: Bring a care partner if you like, since the site welcomes them to class.
Ask about parking, seating and wheelchair access before you go, since the site does not cover them.
Ask whether you can join a series that has already started, because the site does not say.
The Center City class meets at First Presbyterian Church, 201 S. 21st St.

records.notes: Cherry Hill series: the homepage says 8 weeks and the classes page says 10 weeks, but the dates shown are 8 Saturdays (Oct 10 to Nov 28, 2026). The Stapeley older adult site has no street address on the pages read, so it is not listed. The spring listings repeat the fall dates and are unclear, so confirm before signing up. The spring volunteer training is titled 2026 but dated March 20, 2027 on its page. A second address, tangotherapyproject@gmail.com, appears in the volunteer section and is not added. Background check, age and service hour letter rules are not on the training page, so none are recorded. Drop-in and late joining are not stated. Facebook and Instagram were not read.

records.name: Temple Contemporary
records.summary: A free contemporary art gallery on the first floor of Temple's Tyler School of Art and Architecture. It has exhibitions, lectures and public events for anyone to attend.
records.what_you_do: Walk through the free exhibitions during open hours, or come to an evening public event such as a game night or an artist-led party, listed on the gallery's events pages. The gallery lists no public volunteer, docent, class or workshop program.

schedule.text: Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11 am to 6 pm, with free admission. Evening events are scheduled from time to time and listed on the gallery's event pages.

locations.label: Temple Contemporary gallery, Norris Street entrance

first_step.how: Come in during open hours, or check the gallery's events pages and come to a public evening event.
first_step.basis: Free and open to the public during posted hours, with evening events anyone can attend. The page does not mention beginners or a special welcome.
first_step.what_to_expect: Open hours are a self-guided visit: walk through the exhibitions at your own pace at no charge. Evening events such as game nights are more social, with games, drinks and snacks provided.
first_visit_tips: The entrance is on Norris Street, between 12th and 13th streets, inside Tyler School of Art and Architecture.
For access questions, call Tyler at 215-777-9090, since the site does not describe gallery access.
Check the event listing for the date and time before you come to an evening event.

records.notes: The closest interest tag is mural_public_art, since the vocabulary has no gallery or exhibition tag. Newcomer rating changed from 4 to 3 because the page does not mention beginners. Gallery-specific access details are not on the pages read. No volunteer, docent, class or workshop program is listed. Exhibitions run to Dec 5, 2026, and the events page may not show every event.

records.name: Temple University Music Preparatory Division
records.summary: The non-credit music and dance division of Temple's Boyer College of Music and Dance. It teaches music and dance to people of every age, from babies to grown adults.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for private lessons, including Suzuki instruction, or for a group class or ensemble. Programs include group music and dance classes for babies through teens, adult classes and community ensembles, and the Philadelphia String Project for beginning string players. Join the email list for news.

schedule.text: Lessons and classes run through the year for all ages. Individual lesson times are set with your teacher after you enroll, and the site does not list class times.

cost.text: Individual lessons are $40 for 30 minutes, $60 for 45 minutes and $80 for 60 minutes, traditional method, per Temple's course listing. Other arrangements vary, and the application is free. Group class prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Create an account in Temple's non-credit course search, complete the free Individual Music Lessons application, and wait for the office to match you with a teacher. Or join the Music Prep email list.
first_step.basis: Lessons are open to all ages through a free application that carries no obligation, with no audition or placement test, and staff recommend a teacher for each student.
first_step.what_to_expect: Private lessons are one on one with a teacher, in 30, 45 or 60 minute blocks. The course listing suggests 30 minutes for children 12 and under and 45 minutes for older students and adults. New students can start partway through the semester, with the fee prorated.
first_visit_tips: Have your instrument, your experience and your availability ready, because the application asks for them.
Choose a 30, 45 or 60 minute lesson; the listing suggests 30 minutes for children 12 and under.
Ask the office where lessons take place, since the site does not give lesson rooms or times.
Ask about refunds and absences, which are set out in a separate policy document.

records.notes: Two addresses appear on Temple pages: Presser Hall (the site footer, kept here) and a mailing address at 1515 Market Street, Suite 501 on the contact page. Temple's course listing gives the administrative office as 1301 Cecil B. Moore Ave. Confirm before visiting. Lesson rooms, teachers and times are not stated. Status moved to active because Temple's listing for the individual lessons section starts July 1, 2026 and runs to June 30, 2027. Recitals are held at Temple University Center City and livestreamed, per the listing. Suzuki pricing and group class prices are not listed.

records.name: Termite TV Collective
records.summary: A Philadelphia video and media art collective that makes experimental video, shows its work in galleries and screenings, and airs its shows on PhillyCAM. Its Places of Power project uses virtual and augmented reality to tell neighborhood stories.
records.what_you_do: See a free gallery show or screening, watch the collective's shows on PhillyCAM, or ask about its workshops and community projects.

cost.text: Gallery access was free at a past exhibition

first_step.how: Go to a free gallery show or screening, or write to the collective through its website to ask about workshops.
first_step.basis: Past exhibitions and screenings were open to the public at no charge, and the group names a contact person.

records.notes: The group's own site (termite.org) returned empty page text on three attempts, so this record adds no new facts from it. One web search found a PhillyCAM listing for a Termite TV workshop (Collaborative Filmmaking, Mending) with a run from Jan 31 to Apr 2, 2026. The PhillyCAM event page returned HTTP 403 to our fetch tool, so the listing is not used as evidence here. If someone verifies it on phillycam.org, status would move to active. No 2026 screening was found. Workshop details, cost and schedule are unknown.

records.name: The Arc of Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that advocates for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities and their families. It runs parent trainings, Zoom drop-in hours for school planning help, and a youth leadership program.
records.what_you_do: Go to a parent IEP training or a Zoom Ask the Advocate drop-in hour for school planning help, or ask about the youth leadership program for people ages 14 to 21 with disabilities. Families can also send the online intake form to ask for help and connections to other services.

schedule.text: Parent IEP training sessions and Zoom Ask the Advocate drop-in hours are held on dates the site posts and changes. Check the site before you plan to attend.

cost.text: Training fees are not listed on the pages read. Membership is $20 a year and includes event notices and a quarterly newsletter.

first_step.how: Call 215-229-4550 or send the online intake form to ask for help, or join a Zoom Ask the Advocate hour through the site's registration link.
first_step.basis: Drop-in Zoom hours, a listed phone line and an online intake form are open to families and individuals, though the site does not describe a welcome for newcomers.
first_step.what_to_expect: An Ask the Advocate hour is a drop-in call on Zoom, so you can join, ask about school planning and IEPs, and leave when you are done. Parent IEP trainings cover topics such as parent rights, evaluations, writing goals and assistive technology, and some session slides can be downloaded from the site. The site does not say how long sessions last or what the trainings cost.
first_visit_tips: Ask the Advocate hours are on Zoom, so use the registration link on the site to join.
The main office is at 2350 West Westmoreland Street, 19140. The site does not list office hours or transit, so call first.
When you call, ask about sign language, wheelchair access or other accommodations, since the site does not describe them.
Ask about training fees when you register, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: Ask the Advocate hours are drop-in Zoom sessions with a registration link on the homepage. A session set for Oct 13, 2026 was cancelled, per an Oct 5, 2026 notice. The IEP training page lists past sessions only, and its upcoming events link is a placeholder. Youth leadership contact is the advocacy coordinator listed on that page, not copied here. The site has no accessibility or accommodation statement, so none is recorded. The tier 1 access note was removed because it said nothing about access. Membership is $20 a year per the get involved page. Cost level set to unknown because training fees are not listed.

records.name: The Athenaeum of Philadelphia
records.summary: A member supported library, archive and talk space focused on Philadelphia's books, buildings and history. Members can borrow books, and visitors can join small discussion groups and attend talks.
records.what_you_do: Join a book club, a discussion circle, or a Spanish, French or Italian conversation group, take a database course, or go to a talk. Some groups are free, and others show a price on each listing. Research visits are by appointment.

schedule.text: Book clubs, conversation groups and discussion circles meet on set days and times, mostly weekly or monthly, from Monday to Saturday. Talks and courses are listed by date on the events page.

cost.text: Some groups are free, such as the Spanish conversation group. Talks show a price from about $5 to $25, and some listed series show $90 to $120. Student membership is $50 a year, Young Friend membership (ages 18 to 35) is $85 a year, and a day pass to the reading room is $35.

access.notes: The building has an elevator to all three floors and an accessible restroom on the first floor. Visitors who need step free entry can use the ramp from the rear parking lot and ring the intercom to reach the receptionist. One accessible parking space is in the garden, reached from St. James Street.

first_step.how: Open the events page, pick a discussion group, conversation group or talk, and use its registration link. Or call 215-925-2688 to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Groups and talks are listed publicly with dates, prices and sign up links, and a phone line is given for questions. The page does not say who may attend each group.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most groups are small circles that meet on a set day and time, and each listing shows its date, time and price. Visitors can come to the building during posted hours, and research visits need an appointment. The page does not say how long a session lasts or how many people usually come.
first_visit_tips: The Athenaeum is at 219 S. 6th Street, on the east side of Washington Square, below Walnut Street.
Parking garages are about half a block south on 6th Street: Independence Place (self park) and Hopkinson House (valet).
Visiting hours change by day: open until 7 pm on Monday, 10 am to 3 pm on Saturday, and closed on several holidays.
Call 215-925-2688 before you come to ask whether a group is open to non-members, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The Spanish, French and Italian conversation groups are held in those languages, so access.languages carries es, fr and it. Whether non-members may attend most groups and talks is not stated. Member Monday may be for members, but the page does not say. The Oct 12, 2026 database course has no price on the page. Tour booking details and public transit are not on the pages read. Membership levels: Subscriber $160 a year, and Subscriber Plus $260 a year.

records.name: The Chamber Orchestra of Philadelphia
records.summary: A 33 musician chamber orchestra that gives over 30 concerts each season in halls, churches and museums, with talks led by its music director. The public takes part as audience members.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to a concert or a lecture, subscribe to a season, or watch select performances live. The jobs and auditions page has no openings right now and does not describe how auditions work.

schedule.text: The orchestra gives more than 30 subscription, neighborhood and education concerts each season, from fall into late spring. Concerts are often weekend pairs at 4 pm, with some Friday evening shows. Lectures are on Sunday afternoons.

locations.label: Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts (venue named on the Getting Here page)

cost.text: Tickets are sold per concert, and single ticket prices are not listed on the site. Subscribers get 20 percent off single tickets when they call the box office. Lectures at the Philadelphia Ethical Society cost $25 per person.

access.notes: The Getting Here page says the Walnut-Locust station on the Market-Frankford Line is about two blocks from the Kimmel Center. Buses 9, 21, 32 and 42 are listed as accessible.

first_step.how: Buy a single ticket to any concert online or by calling the box office at (215) 545-1739, or sign up on the site for news and offers.
first_step.basis: Concerts and lectures are open to the public with a ticket, and the site has a clear way to buy in, though it has no first-timer guide.
first_step.what_to_expect: Concerts are given in different places, including halls, churches, museums and cloisters, so check the venue on your ticket. Weekend concerts listed on the site start at 4 pm. Lectures at the Philadelphia Ethical Society run on Sunday afternoons at 2:30 pm and cost $25 per person.
first_visit_tips: Check the venue on your ticket before you go, since concerts move between halls, churches and museums.
If you drive to the Kimmel Center, the garage entrance is just south of the Broad Street entrance, and you can only reach it by driving south on Broad Street.
Walnut-Locust station is about two blocks away, and buses 9, 21, 32 and 42 run nearby.
Call the box office at (215) 545-1739 to ask about seating or access, since the site does not describe them.

records.notes: community_band is the closest music tag. The orchestra is professional and lists no community player roles. The homepage says concerts take place in several venues; the Getting Here page names only the Kimmel Center, so it is listed as a venue, but check each ticket. The employment page lists no openings. The box office number (215) 545-1739 is separate from the general number on the record. No student, senior, rush or free tickets are listed.

records.name: PhillyCAM
records.summary: A Philadelphia community media center that teaches media skills and makes local programs for cable TV, FM radio and the web. Some of its workshops are free and open to the public, and it offers member orientation sessions.
records.what_you_do: Take a free media workshop, such as acting for the camera, or attend an orientation session to learn about the center and its radio and TV programs.

schedule.text: Free workshops and orientation sessions are scheduled by date and listed on the site, with times in each listing. Some are held online.

cost.text: The listed workshops are free. Membership fees are not stated on the site.

first_step.how: Log in to the center's member system and register for a free workshop on the events list.
first_step.basis: Free workshops are open to the public and listed with dates, and the site has a membership link and a sign up step, though the page does not say whether drop in is allowed.
first_step.what_to_expect: Workshops are hands-on sessions in media skills, such as acting for the camera. Orientation sessions introduce newcomers to the center's radio and TV work, and a radio orientation is held online.
first_visit_tips: Log in to the member system before the workshop date, because registration happens there.
The office is at 699 Ranstead Street, Suite 1, near 7th Street between Market and Chestnut streets.
Hours are on the site's Directions and Hours page. Call 267-639-5481 to check before you come.

records.notes: New group, not in this batch. Found as the community media partner named in the Termite TV Collective listing. The verdict is based on the homepage only; the Directions and Hours page and member pages were not read. The homepage lists no Termite TV items. Kind is set to program because the page does not say whether the center is a nonprofit. Membership fees and drop in rules are not stated. A Termite TV workshop listing on phillycam.org returned HTTP 403, so it is not used here.

notes: Batch of 7 groups. Seven batch records updated to research_tier 2, plus one new record (PhillyCAM, the media partner named in the Termite TV listing). Verdicts: publish 8. Budget: 35 of 60 fetches and 1 of 1 WebSearch. Termite TV Collective: termite.org returned empty page text on three attempts, so its record rests on earlier sources plus one search. Tango Therapy Project peer page (13 names) dispositions: Tango Mercurio, Washington DC area, out of area; Spirit Rising, Bucks County, out of area; Philly NeuroArts Network, a directory page with no meeting or join details; Anyone Can Move, describes a Philadelphia adaptive movement program, but its page gives no address, schedule, cost or join step, so not a record yet; Dance for Parkinson's, a New York based national program with no Philadelphia class listed; Rock Steady Boxing, an Indiana based national program with no Philadelphia location listed; Power for Parkinson's, a Texas based program with no Philadelphia class listed; Katz JCC Parkinson's Connection, in Cherry Hill NJ, outside the city, not fetched; Dan Aaron Stay Fit Clinic, an Arcadia University clinic outside the city, not fetched; Parkinson's Foundation, a national charity, not fetched; MDT Education Solutions, a company, not fetched; the University of Pennsylvania Parkinson's center, a medical center with no usable link on the list. Partner names without links on the Athenaeum and Chamber pages (Preservation Alliance, Opera Philadelphia, Philadelphia Ethical Society) were not listed. Newcomer ratings: Temple Contemporary changed from 4 to 3 (no beginner language on the page); Tango Therapy raised from 2 to 3 (register links now found). Closest-fit tags kept and explained in record notes: Temple Contemporary (mural_public_art) and Chamber Orchestra (community_band). Mistake: one call went to a session tool (read_widget_context) that is outside the allowed tool set. It returned a generic message, and nothing from it was used.
